Eli: Heads-up — last night we saw a burst of ECC/Xid noise in eu-west-1 that caused ~40 noisy alerts across different nodes in the same rack. Most were transient but Prometheus rules fired repeatedly and triggered several automated drains.
Maria: Ugh. Do we know if it's a single flaky card or an infra/network event? Any correlation with driver/kernel? :thinking:
Eli: Preliminary: kernel stayed the same, DCGM exporter showed short ECC spikes on multiple hosts but with identical card serials appearing across ~6 hosts (suggests noisy telemetry rather than physical card flipping). Also DCGM sample_rate jumped during our nightly snapshot job window.
Jing: That matches a hypothesis we've discussed — sampling bursts + per-host rules = alert storm. We should avoid draining on single short spikes.
Sam: Proposed fix? Lower sensitivity on rules or longer sliding windows? Both have trade-offs.
Eli: I'd like to propose an aggregation/rollup layer in front of alert evaluation:
- ingest raw DCGM metrics (dcgm_ecc_errors_total, dcgm_xid_errors_total) into a short-lived aggregator (stateless service or small Prometheus rewrite) that groups by GPU serial and region, computes a "gpu_alert_score" over a configurable window, and emits a single aggregated metric per GPU: `redwood_gpu_alert_score{gpu_serial, region}`
- Use that score in Prom rules instead of raw counters (threshold + hysteresis)
- Keep per-host raw alerts for debugging (low-severity) but do not trigger drains from them
Eli: Sketch of a recording rule we could use after aggregation (pseudocode):
```
# aggregator output: redwood_gpu_alert_score{gpu_serial="...", region="eu-west-1"}
record: redwood_gpu_alert_score:avg_2m
expr: avg_over_time(redwood_gpu_alert_score[2m])
```
Maria: Sounds reasonable. A few concerns:
- Latency: adding an aggregation hop could add 30-60s. Will that violate SLOs for real failures?
- Edge cases: what if a physical card is failing and multiple hosts show the same serial because of snapshot bug? We need a way to still escalate.
Jing: On the edge cases — aggregator should produce both a short-term and long-term score (e.g., 30s and 5m windows). Short-term triggers a page if above high threshold + corroborated by system metrics (GPU temperature/fan/driver logs). Long-term triggers automated drain.
Sam: Implementation options:
- small Go service consuming Prom remote_write or scraping DCGM push endpoints, computing rollups, writing to Prom remote_write or Pushgateway
- implement within Prometheus as a recording job using relabeling and a custom exporter script per region (less infra but hackier)
Eli: I'm leaning to a tiny aggregator service (k8s deployment per region) so we can ship better instrumentation and backfills. It also lets us do cardinality bounding (cap the number of gpu_serials we keep in memory) and probabilistic dedup for storms.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: created ticket INFRA-2317 for "gpu alert aggregation service (canary)" assigned to @Eli
Oncall: Important: keep a manual override flag for accelerations (override=false => normal aggregation, override=true => bypass aggregator and run old rules). We should also keep full logs of raw DCGM timeseries for 30d before aggregation rollouts.
Maria: Test plan suggestion:
- Canary in eu-central-1 with ~20 nodes, run aggregator in shadow mode (emit aggregated metrics but do NOT use them for alerting)
- After 1 week, flip canary to use aggregated scores for alert evaluation in a single alertgroup
- Monitor false negatives vs false positives with a labeled evaluation set (historic incidents replay)
Jing: Also add an integration test that replays past noisy windows (we have recordings from 2024-11-07) and assert that alerts drop by >70% while real failures still cause a page.
Eli: Ops list / action items:
1) Eli: prototype aggregator binary + docker image (1d)
2) Maria: create shadow alert group + dashboard panels for redwood_gpu_alert_score (2d)
3) Jing: assemble replay dataset and test harness (3d)
4) Sam: update drain automation to require long-term score > X AND corroboration (5d)
5) Team: schedule canary rollout in eu-central-1 and track MTTI/MTTR metrics
Maria: Fine to go ahead on the prototype. Please keep the score calculation formula simple at first (weighted sum of normalized signals: ECC*2 + XID*3 + temp_spike*1).
Eli: Will do. I'll drop the initial PR with a README and a sample Prom remote_write config. Expect a draft in this thread by EOD.
Sam: One more note — add MIG awareness: the aggregator must map NVML GPU index to MIG instance id and only roll up across the same MIG instance.
Eli: Noted. Thanks all :thumbsup:
ops-bot: ticket INFRA-2317 updated: initial PR link will be posted here.
Oncall: Great work. Keep the runbook updated so oncall knows when to bypass aggregator for urgent infra events.
